chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from some of our companions, raising it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him):

Regarding a man who swore to weigh an elephant, so they brought it to him. He said, 'Why do you swear by what you cannot do?' I said, 'I have been tested.' So he ordered a large vessel containing reeds, and much reed was taken out of it. Then he taught the coloring of the water to the extent that the coloring of the water was known before the reeds were removed. Then he placed the elephant in it until it returned to the measure to which the coloring of the water had first reached. Then he ordered that the reeds which were removed be weighed. When they were weighed, he said, 'This is the weight of the elephant.'

And he said regarding a man who was bound, who swore that he would not leave his place until he knew the weight of his shackle. So he ordered that his foot be placed in a bowl containing water. When he knew its measure with his foot placed in it, he then raised the shackle to his knee. Then he knew the measure of its coloring. Then he ordered that weights be thrown into the water until the water returned to the measure of what the shackle was in the water. When the water became upon that coloring which it was, and the shackle was in the water, he looked at how much the weight that was thrown into the water was. When he weighed it, he said, 'This is the weight of your shackle.'

And he said: A man was sitting with five loaves of bread before him. Another man came with three loaves and threw them with him. Then a man came with nothing and sat with them, and they ate. When they finished, he threw eight dirhams to them and left. The owner of the five said to the owner of the three, 'Take three dirhams and go.' He said, 'I do not see less than half.' He said, 'Do not do that.' So he swore that he would not be satisfied with less than half. So they went up to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) and narrated their story to him.

He said, 'How many do you have?' He said, 'Five.' He said, 'These are fifteen.' And he said to the other, 'How many do you have?' He said, 'Three.' He said, 'These are nine, and that is four, and twenty-eight. The share of each is eight. So for the owner of the three, nine: he ate eight, so only one remains for him. And for the owner of the five, fifteen: he ate eight, and seven remain for him.'

key_terms.صَبْغ: Coloring/dyeing (used here to indicate water level/displacement)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali determine the weight of an elephant or a shackle without a scale, and how is bread payment divided among contributors?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s practical jurisprudence (*fiqh*) through three distinct narratives demonstrating the application of *'ilm al-halaf* (knowledge of oaths) to fulfill conditional vows. The first two cases showcase ingenious physical methods—water displacement and coloring—to determine the weight of an elephant and a shackle without direct weighing, while the third establishes the principle of proportional distribution (*nisab*) in shared resources, correcting the common misconception of equal division. These examples underscore the Shia scholarly emphasis on rational deduction and equitable justice in resolving complex legal scenarios.
